However, the company also reported a substantial net loss of $709 million and $846 million in quarterly interest expenses. To navigate these financial challenges, CoreWeave is shifting towards customer prepayments and shorter contracts, which could enhance cash flow while leveraging existing infrastructure more effectively [CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth].

This advancement allows corporate leaders to assign a variety of tasks to Genie, which can analyze data and provide insights without supervision. CEO Ali Ghodsi demonstrated the agent's capabilities by showcasing its analysis of employee satisfaction surveys and sales pitches, highlighting its potential to improve decision-making processes within organizations [Databricks’ new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth].

article_hits.content: In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses. On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. article_hits.title: Siri co-founder backs Helix for its voice ID tech
article_hits.content: For years, websites have relied on technology like CAPTCHA to prove that the user on the other end is human. More recently, social media platforms have turned to photos or videos to verify users’ identities. Now, a startup called Helix is betting that voice technology can do the same job, without requiring users to hand over sensitive personal information. The voice technology, which can run directly on a user’s device, has attracted backing from Siri co-founder Dag Kittlaus, who will also act as an advisor. The company raised $6 million in funding in a round led by Chicago Ventures, with participation from BAM Ventures, Aglaé Ventures, Corazon Capital, Tusk Ventures, Yonder Ventures, Rule30, and Brown Alumni Group. The startup was founded by Alex Oberg, Anna Dorofiyenko, and Mike Hall in 2025. article_hits.title: Databricks’ new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth
article_hits.content: Databricks on Wednesday unveiled an updated version of its AI agent Genie, which can now perform multi-step jobs that take extended work to finish.  It does this through an ontology that Databricks built to give Genie the context it needs from the information that customers store on the Databricks platform. Corporate leaders can now assign the agent a wide range of tasks, and it will complete them unsupervised, the company says. To prove the point, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi showed me how he uses it internally. Instead of a product demo, he fired up his actual agent and walked me through his most recent chats and charts. He showed me how it analyzed the parts of an employee satisfaction survey where the company didn’t score well, and how it helped him rate (and discard) fixes for those low scores that some executives suggested. article_hits.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth
article_hits.content: CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings , reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices. The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue. CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense. “We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call.
